title: The Impact of Ecological Momentary Assessment Frequency on Data Characteristics and Predictive Utility
titleZh: 生态瞬时评估频率对数据特征与预测效用的影响
abstract: This study investigated whether assessing the frequency of smartphone-based ecological momentary assessments (EMAs) impacts stress and affect and their predictive utility for health behaviors in ways that are consistent with evidence of measurement reactivity (e.g., self-enhancement motives, practice effects, fatigue). Participants ( N = 460; 77% female) were randomized to different EMA frequencies. More frequent EMAs were associated with lower mean stress and anger, and higher mean happiness, but patterns of effects were not consistent with measurement reactivity expectations. Instead, results align more with assumptions that more data improves measurement precision than with expectations for measurement reactivity. Analyses revealed no substantive effects of assessment frequency on health behavior outcomes, and although assessment frequency sometimes moderated associations between affect and stress on health behaviors, effect sizes were trivial. The study highlights the importance of optimizing assessment frequency in EMA study designs to capture real-time dynamics rather than to mitigate measurement reactivity.
